# Gevurah Critique — ffmpeg Fallback Safety and Truth

The Awtsmoos gives limitless creation, but Awtsmoos.com binds the proof service to localhost, bounded names, bounded bytes, explicit counts, and no shell injection at the gate.

1. Never accept arbitrary output paths from the browser.
2. Session IDs must be generated server-side or validated to a strict safe alphabet.
3. Frame filenames derive only from integer indices.
4. Every frame upload has a maximum byte size.
5. WAV upload has a bounded maximum size sufficient for the 180-second acceptance soundtrack.
6. ffmpeg command arguments must be an argv list, never a shell command string.
7. Finalize must require exactly the expected frame count before encoding.
8. Width/height/fps/duration must be numeric and bounded.
9. Browser uploader must surface failed frame index and HTTP response.
10. No entire-film in-memory frame accumulation.
11. Audio is optional only for explicit video-only mode; acceptance proof requires audio.
12. Output evidence path is controlled by server and remains beneath the proof media root.
13. Temporary sessions must be separable from final artifacts.
14. Browser-side frame renderer remains canonical seconds; no timing translation duplication.
15. ffmpeg output must still be independently ffprobed after service finalization.
16. This fallback must be clearly labeled native/local ffmpeg; never misrepresented as browser-only WebCodecs.
17. Keep each new source file below 120 lines; split HTTP handler, session model, ffmpeg runner, browser uploader, WAV encoder, and page orchestration.
